FIELD NOTE 002 · THE RING THAT WILL NOT CLOSE · NOVEMBER 2026

The error has to
live somewhere.

Twelve pure fifths cannot close a circle. The ring has to choose where to fail, and some ears make it keep the choice.

THE OBSERVATION
Some rules cannot be obeyed.
The failure has a shape.
Stack twelve pure fifths and you overshoot seven octaves by 23.46 cents, about a quarter of a semitone. That gap is the Pythagorean comma, and musicians have been negotiating with it for two and a half thousand years.
The Ring gives twelve voices one instruction each: be a pure fifth above the voice to your left. Because the voices sit on a circle, the last voice’s left neighbour is the first. Followed all the way round, the instruction asks pitch to come back to itself plus a comma. It can’t. The errors on the twelve fifths must add up to −23.46 cents, always. The only open question is where that error lives.
The rule is one sentence. The contradiction is two percent of an octave.
Everything else is the shape of the failure.
Which shape depends on something the rule never mentions: how much a fifth minds being out of tune. If discomfort grows with the square of the error, the cheapest answer spreads the comma evenly, with every fifth 1.955 cents flat. That is twelve-tone equal temperament. If small errors are nearly free and large ones barely worse, the cheapest answer piles the whole comma onto one fifth. Eleven are pure and one is a wolf.
Roughness, the beating a listener actually hears, behaves like the second kind near a pure fifth. Under it, equal temperament is not a resting place. Start the ring there with a hundredth of a cent of noise and within a minute the comma gathers into one wolf, on an edge the noise chose. Push a voice and the wolf moves to where you pushed, then stays. A quadratic ring forgets every push. A roughness ring keeps a record of the last one.


WHAT THE MODEL SAYS
Discomfort is the dial.
Each voice has a pitch class θ in cents. The error on fifth i is εᵢ = θᵢ₊₁ − θᵢ − 701.955, wrapped into (−600, 600]. Around the ring the errors always sum to −23.46 + 1200k cents. The whole number k counts windings. Changing it would take one pair of neighbours through a minor second or a minor ninth, and ordinary relaxation never does that.
Each voice moves to ease the discomfort on the two fifths it belongs to. A listening weight λ sets whom it listens to. On this page it is ½: listening is mutual, and the ring slides downhill on its total discomfort with its average pitch fixed. In the full Ring λ can go to 1, so each voice follows only its left neighbour. Then the whole ring drifts in pitch at a steady rate while the wolf stays on its edge. One-way listening carries force around the ring, not error, and the wolf and the near-pure fifths settle where they pull equally hard. So the ring moves as a body and the wolf is left behind as a landmark.
The full Ring also has a tuner mode, which makes listening part of the rule: only the fifth being heard may retune. Direction matters. When the window and the retuning move the same way, the tuner meets the full wolf at every fifth it reaches, tunes it pure, and finds it waiting at the next. Moving the other way, the tuner meets the wolf once a lap, one fifth further back each time. A mutual tuner splits whatever it finds in half, one half ahead and one behind, and after a few laps the ring is close to equal temperament. A one-sided tuner carries the wolf. A two-sided tuner dissolves it.
None of this is a claim about the history of tuning. Equal temperament and the single wolf are the only resting states a single-exponent cost produces. Meantone and the well-temperaments optimise something else, and they do not appear here.


Equations, parameters & numerical method
dθᵢ/dt = R · [(1 − λ)·gᵢ·F(εᵢ) − λ·gᵢ₋₁·F(εᵢ₋₁)]
F = D′ is the slope of the discomfort curve. On this page λ = ½, R = 1 per second, every gᵢ = 1, no voice is pinned and noise is zero. In the full Ring’s tuner mode, gᵢ = 3 on the fifth being heard and 0 elsewhere; its noise defaults to 0.01 cents·√s per voice and can be set to zero.
Quadratic: D = ε²/2. Roughness: the Sethares sensory dissonance of the sounding pair (two six-harmonic tones, amplitudes 0.88ᵏ⁻¹, lower voice at 220·√2 Hz, the middle of the A3 octave) as a function of the fifth’s mistuning, smoothed with a 0.5-cent Gaussian so the pure fifth has finite stiffness. Its slope is scaled so the largest force within ±60 cents is 12. One curve serves every edge.
The page starts from equal temperament. “Push” adds 20 cents to voice 3. The model advances in fixed frames of 1/60 s, each split into explicit Euler steps of at most 4 ms and capped at 2 cents per step, the same stepping the archived checks use. If the tab drops frames, the ring slows rather than catching up. Each run stops at 40 simulated seconds.
Sound plays the fifth being heard: voice w at its pitch class above 220 Hz, and the voice above it a fifth higher, mistuned by εw, in the same six-harmonic timbre the roughness is computed from. Gains are 0.5 and 0.42 under a fixed 0.35 master. The window moves on every 2 seconds while the ring runs or sound is on; it never changes the dynamics. Hidden tabs and navigation pause the ring and stop sound.
The ring core is the archived 190-line file, byte for byte; this page’s adapter only sets the preset and the parameters above.


EVIDENCE / LIMITS
A claim you can check.
Push voice 3 sharp by 20 cents from equal temperament and release. After 40 seconds the quadratic ring has every fifth back between −1.95 and −1.96 cents. The roughness ring holds a −19.6-cent wolf on fifth 3, where the push was, with −0.35 cents on each of the other eleven. Both still sum to −23.46. That is the experiment above, run to the end.
The archived checks go further than this page. Started in equal temperament with 0.01-cent noise, the roughness ring condenses to one wolf within about 45 seconds, on fifth 2, 7 and 5 for three different noise seeds. A comma split evenly between two fifths holds unchanged for 300 seconds with no noise and merges into one wolf within 60 seconds once noise is on: the even split is a balance point, and noise picks the side. With each voice following its left neighbour, the quadratic ring rises 1.955 cents a second and the roughness ring 6.06, while the wolf stays on fifth 5. With mutual listening the drift is zero.
Those are numerical results for the model as built, not measurements of instruments or players. The roughness curve uses the Sethares (1993) formula as Claude recalled it, and its parameters were not checked against the paper. The smoothing matters too. At a sharper 0.05 cents, the Round 3 runs saw several partial wolves still merging after 400 seconds, so whether a sharper ear would hold more than one wolf is open. The model scores only the twelve neighbouring fifths, not the 66 intervals twelve voices make together, which is why the page plays one fifth at a time.
No listener study has been run. Whether the wolf’s arrival is unmistakable, whether forgetting and remembering are felt, and whether drift sounds like the ground moving are hopes, not results. In the full Ring, with tuner mode off, try All twelve at once and say where the wolf is. The prediction is that nobody can. The journal does not claim scientific novelty or peer review.
This page’s model checks rerun the push test through the page’s own adapter, confirm the sum never moves and the reset is exact. The archived checks cover the push test, the collapse of equal temperament, the even split, drift and tuner mode; the checks built into the full Ring are a reduced subset of them. The implementation record keeps what the rules demonstrably do apart from what a listener is hoped to hear, and records what did not go as predicted. The verification record separates automated browser checks from device-testing gaps. Real phone audio, speaker audibility and assistive-technology use still need hands-on testing.


WHERE THIS CAME FROM
An instrument the review changed.
The Ring That Will Not Close was proposed and built by Claude (Anthropic) in Study 02, The Question That Changes, a collaborative study initiated, facilitated and evaluated by James Stewart. The study began with one question: what is the smallest set of rules from which something unexpectedly rich can emerge? ChatGPT, Gemini and Grok took part in the broader study and reviewed the Ring anonymously. That does not make them its coauthors.
Claude’s first proposal, on 20 October 2026, turned the question around. In Life or Rule 110 the rule is always obeyed, and richness is what obeying it produces. The Ring was meant to be rich because its rule cannot be obeyed. It also promised more than it could deliver: a comma that could be launched and chased around the ring like a particle.
The reviewers took that promise apart from three directions. ChatGPT showed that a flat cost produces no motion at all, and that the curve which gathers the comma also pins it in place. Gemini computed the barrier between neighbouring wolf positions and noticed that the rule had been written two ways, one-way and mutual, which behave differently. Grok corrected the arithmetic of which ring sizes nearly close. Only 53 does.
In Round 3, on 21 October, Claude ran twelve numbers in a loop against each critique, withdrew the mobile comma, and found what replaced it. Under real roughness the comma is not a particle but a deposit, left where it was last put. One-way listening drifts the whole ring instead of moving the wolf, a result none of the reviewers had predicted. The question changed with it: what is the smallest rule that cannot be obeyed, and what selects among the ways of failing it?
Round 4, the same day, built the instrument and corrected Round 3 once more. Round 3 had said a tuner would never hear the wolf; the build showed the tuner hears it at every step or once a lap, depending on direction. Tuner mode adapts an idea about attention from Cæsura, another proposal in the study that Claude reviewed in Round 2.
This journal is a presentation of that instrument, not a replacement for it or its record. Experiment version: ring-journal-1. The archived ring core is used unchanged.
